Group plots · filters · 2026-11-21

The top 60 MarketSmith industry groups (each chart is MSI's own group index) · every Group Flag Charts attribute as a filter, plus the filters the study found to hold up · last candle 19 Nov 2026
Market: Confirmed Uptrend — a screen of groups, not a recommendation. Display only: no Tier 1 gate or Tier 2 weight is changed.
What the research found (group_filter_study.py → data/group_filter_study_results.md): equal-weight indices for ~175 groups from ~3,600 NSE stocks, 2013-2026; flagged groups' next 10/20-session return minus the market's, averaged over non-overlapping dates; earlier half (to 2019) vs later half (2020+) must agree. Held up: closeness to the 1-year high, breadth (% of members above their 50-/200-DMA, % near their 52-week high), the Unfluke-style 1-99 rating, RS line at a 250-day high, the trend template on the group index, above the 20 EMA. Did not hold up: a "pullback to the 20 EMA inside a strong group" (≈0 at 10 sessions, negative at 20), the 15-day rating rise (weak and unstable), RS-leads-price (too few cases).
Preset (combination)Result vs the other groups (excess return, flagged − unflagged)
★ Best: trend template on the group index+0.72% / 10 sessions (t 5.9), +1.50% / 20 sessions (t 6.2) vs the other groups; same sign in both halves; ~14 of 174 groups a day
Trend template + ≥ 50% members > 200-DMA+0.73% / 10 (t 5.4), +1.42% / 20 (t 5.3) — adding breadth did not improve on the trend template alone
Near 1y high + ≥ 60% members > 50-DMA+0.69% / 10 (t 5.9), +1.10% / 20 (t 4.8); same sign in both halves; ~24 groups a day
Rating ≥ 90 + above 20 EMA+0.66% / 10 (t 4.3), +1.24% / 20 (t 3.5); same sign in both halves
Rating ≥ 80 + ≥ 60% members > 50-DMA+0.56% / 10 (t 4.1), +0.98% / 20 (t 3.5)
Rating ≥ 80 + RS line high+0.98% / 10 (t 4.5) but at 20 sessions the earlier half was −0.22%: unstable; only ~3 groups a day
⚠️ Limits: today's group membership is applied to the past (survivorship); equal-weight is not MSI's own group index; early years have fewer priced stocks per group; the MSI group-rank history exists only since June 2026 and is not part of the test. These are leads for a forward test, not rules. The Unfluke-style readings on MSI's own index (volatility, ADX, NR4/NR7, inside bar) cannot be tested that way — they have no high/low in the study index — so they are shown, not claimed.

Entry flags under the candles — what each one means
▲P Pocket pivot — an early buy inside a base, or off the 10-day in an uptrend, before the obvious breakout (Morales & Kacher). An up day (close above the prior close) whose volume is at least the largest down-day volume of the prior 10 sessions, closing above the 50-day average, with the day's low right at or just below the 10-day average (at most 1% above it) and the close back above the 10-day.
▲G Gap-up buy point — opens above the prior day's high; the gap from the prior close is at least 0.75× the average true range of the previous 40 sessions; volume is at least 1.5× its 50-day average; and the day's range comes within 5% of the base high. Stop = the gap day's low.
▲B Breakout — the first close above the base high (the highest high of the prior 6 months, set at least 3 weeks earlier) on volume at least 1.5× its 50-day average — the book's 50%-above-average breakout rule.
△ Not a buy — a pocket pivot or gap that breaks one of the book's rules — extended (low more than 1% above the 10-day), closed below the 10-day, below the 50-day, a downtrend (50-day falling, under the 200-day), the lower third of the base, wedging up on lighter volume, a V-shaped drop to the 20-day that never touched the 50-day, a wide and loose base (deeper than 50% or weekly swings of 10%+), or a gap extended more than 5% above the base high or still inside the base. Shown for the last 60 sessions only.
The flags are judged on SIMPLE moving averages, as in the book's charts: the 10-day (location, extended) and 50-day (above it), plus the 20-day (V-shape) and 200-day (downtrend). Every chart shows the 10- and 50-day lines — dotted where the page's own lines are EMAs.
Hover a marker to see its numbers, whether the day closed in the upper half of its range (the book calls a mid-range close weak) and whether trading was quiet before it. The thresholds freeze a discretionary book (Trade Like an O'Neil Disciple, ch. 5) into rules: reading aids, not tested signals. On NSE only the breakout-day versions are measured — gap-ups helped (42.3% vs 34.5% reached +20% in 60 days); pocket-pivot volume barely did, because 77% of breakouts have it.
